title: Jude and the Letters
premise: Edmund Yarrow, once the most sought-after wedding planner on the coast, has spent seven years hiding behind other people's happily-ever-afters since her own engagement collapsed in scandal. When a freak snowstorm traps her at a remote island inn with Theo Marchetti—the rival planner who stole her business—and Jude Calloway, the fiancé who vanished the night before their wedding, three buried truths surface faster than the ferry can return. As power plays from their shared past unravel, Edmund learns Jude left not from betrayal but to protect her from his family's corrupt empire, and that Theo's rivalry was a desperate bid for her attention. By the last ferry of the season, Edmund must choose between the safe invisibility she's built and a visible, imperfect love—forgiving herself first.
about_author: Elodie Delacroix is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade watching love arrive in ballrooms and leave in parking lots. She writes from a drafty cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she keeps every letter she never sent.

chapters.title: The Last Booking
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Seven years after her own wedding fell apart, Edmund Yarrow plans flawless weddings for strangers while refusing her sister's plea to attend one as a guest. When she accepts a lucrative off-season job on Greyfriar Island, she discovers the rival planner hired alongside her is Theo Marchetti—and the groom is Jude Calloway. Beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Salt and Snow
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives on the island determined to finally beat Edmund at her own game, carrying guilt over how he won their old turf war. A reconnaissance walk to the venue ends with him face-to-face with Edmund in the boathouse, where old wounds spark into sharp, electric banter. Beat: rivalry revealed as something rawer than competition.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The storm hits early; the ferry stops running, the wedding party scatters, and Edmund, Theo, and Jude are stranded together at the inn when the generator fails. Candlelight and cold force proximity, and Jude says her name for the first time in seven years. Beat: the past knocks, and there is nowhere to hide.

chapters.title: Letters Unsent
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Trapped upstairs, Jude confesses he wrote Edmund letters for years after leaving—letters his family intercepted—and produces one he kept hidden in his coat. Reading it, Edmund learns he fled because his father threatened to destroy her career. Beat: loyalty reframed as a cage; grief with a new shape.

chapters.title: The Innkeeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Digging through the inn's records to salvage the wedding logistics, Theo uncovers proof that Jude's family company quietly bought the island—and that the wedding itself is a laundering scheme. He must decide whether exposing it saves Edmund or destroys the man she might still love. Beat: truth becomes a weapon with a cost.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Said
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Confronting Theo about the ledger, Edmund instead hears him admit the rivalry was always about her—that winning her business was the only way he knew to stay in her life. Shaken, she faces her reflection and admits she chose invisibility long before anyone forced it on her. Beat: the enemy becomes a mirror.

chapters.title: Power Corrupts the Guest List
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude's father arrives by helicopter, breaking the storm's isolation, and demands the wedding proceed as cover. Jude publicly refuses for the first time in his life, forfeiting his inheritance and his name. Beat: climax of the power theme—loyalty to truth over blood.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the storm's final hours, all three collide: Jude asks for a future, Theo asks for honesty, and Edmund realizes she cannot answer either until she forgives the woman who waited too long to ask questions. She walks out into the snow alone to decide. Beat: emotional climax; forgiveness begins inward.

chapters.title: First Ferry Out
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Morning breaks clear. The last ferry of the season loads at dawn: the wedding cancelled, the guests departing, the Calloway empire under federal inquiry thanks to the ledger. On the dock, Edmund hands Theo the first honest contract of her career—a partnership, signed freely. Beat: release; rivalry transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: Jude and the Letters
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. One year later, Edmund plans no weddings but runs a small studio restoring old letters for families—including, slowly, the ones Jude never got to send. On the same dock, she boards the first ferry of the new season beside him, visible at last. Beat: resolution; memory kept, love in present tense.
